definitions.explanation: A system of government in which the head of state is elected or appointed rather than inheriting the position, and sovereignty rests with the people.

examples.japanese: フランスは{共和制|きょうわせい}の{国|くに}だ。
{革命|かくめい}の{後|あと}、{共和制|きょうわせい}が{樹立|じゅりつ}された。
examples.english: After the revolution, a republic was established.

examples.japanese: {君主制|くんしゅせい}から{共和制|きょうわせい}への{移行|いこう}は{平和的|へいわてき}に{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: The transition from monarchy to republic was carried out peacefully.

notes:
Compound of {共和|きょうわ} (republic/republican) and {制|せい} (system). The {制|せい} suffix indicates a system of governance, as in {君主制|くんしゅせい} (monarchy) or {民主制|みんしゅせい} (democracy).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {共和制|きょうわせい}を{樹立|じゅりつ}する: to establish a republic
- {共和制|きょうわせい}の{国|くに}: a republican nation
- {共和制|きょうわせい}に{移行|いこう}する: to transition to a republic
- {大統領|だいとうりょう}{共和制|きょうわせい}: presidential republic

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {共和国|きょうわこく}: republic (as a country) — refers to a specific republican nation, while {共和制|きょうわせい} refers to the system itself
- {君主制|くんしゅせい}: monarchy — government headed by a hereditary ruler, the opposite system
- {民主制|みんしゅせい}: democracy — government by the people, can coexist with {共和制|きょうわせい}
- {立憲制|りっけんせい}: constitutional government — government based on a constitution
